0.long_answer: The disorder described is Shapiro syndrome. It is an extremely rare condition characterized by paroxysmal hypothermia and hyperhidrosis, resulting from hypothalamic dysfunction of thermoregulation. Often, patients experience unpredictable episodes of low body temperature and excessive sweating. Due to the similarities in autonomic disturbances, especially in terms of dysregulated body temperature control, it can sometimes be mistaken for autoimmune encephalitis. Additionally, Shapiro syndrome may be associated with the agenesis of the corpus callosum, although this is not always present.
